labelled_by: Claude (draft, researched live via WebFetch/WebSearch 2026-09-27) -- NOT an independent human researcher; needs human review before being treated as frozen ground truth.
rules: Label only what the website states. No outside knowledge. Copy quotes exactly. If pages disagree, record both as conflicting. If the site does not say, use not_found.
review_notes: Quotes were retrieved via an AI-summarizing fetch tool rather than raw HTML, so wording is presented as verbatim by that tool but could not be independently re-verified byte-for-byte; treat quotes as close paraphrase-quality. ISO/SOC2 badges on the about page were described as displayed logos, not linked to a specific certificate number or scope -- flagged for human re-check. named_customers list trimmed to a representative subset; many more logos/case studies exist on razorpay.com/customer-stories and /case-studies. No on-site page was found that names specific competitor companies (the one 'vs other payment gateways' blog post explicitly avoids naming real competitors, using 'Gateway A/B' instead), so comparisons.named_alternatives is not_found. B-51 (2026-09-27), customers.segments re-checked via a fresh live WebFetch: the original value/evidence here was a paraphrase description ('Homepage markets to India's businesses across...'), not text copied verbatim from the page -- a labelling error, since this project's own rule 3 requires literal quotes. The only quotable homepage material actually found ('E-Commerce | Education | BFSI | SaaS | Freelancer') is an industry-vertical tab strip, already captured faithfully by customers.industries below; no separate statement distinguishes a customer TYPE (company size, buyer role, etc.), which is what this field means. Corrected to not_found per rule 4 (prefer not_found over guessing) rather than reuse industries content under a different field name.
